result.summary: The intersection is equipped with high-visibility continental crosswalks and sidewalks, controlled by overhead traffic signals. However, the environment lacks dedicated pedestrian signals and features a wide roadway that may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Missing pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible at the intersection, requiring pedestrians to rely on vehicle signals which may not provide adequate clearance time.

hazards.name: Wide roadway exposure
hazards.description: The wide, multi-lane one-way street increases the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic without a refuge island.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on crossing time remaining.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a head start before vehicles get a green light, reducing conflicts with turning traffic.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility zebra crosswalks and overhead traffic signals, providing a basic level of pedestrian infrastructure. However, the wide roadway creates a long unprotected crossing distance, increasing pedestrian exposure to vehicle traffic.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians are exposed to traffic for a significant duration due to the wide roadway and lack of a median refuge.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the intersection crossing the main road

hazards.name: Wide lane geometry
hazards.description: The wide, open road design may encourage higher vehicle speeds, increasing risk to pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to provide a safe waiting area and allow for two-stage crossing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The image shows a two-lane urban street with a marked high-visibility crosswalk and sidewalks on both sides. While basic pedestrian infrastructure is present, the crossing lacks active traffic control or speed-calming measures to protect pedestrians from through traffic.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross two lanes of traffic without the protection of a visible signal or stop sign for approaching vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground at the marked crosswalk

hazards.name: Wide travel lanes
hazards.description: The width of the roadway and lack of physical narrowing may encourage higher vehicle speeds through the crossing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Raised Crosswalk
interventions.description: Elevate the crosswalk to the level of the sidewalk to physically slow vehicles and increase pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-activated flashing lights to alert drivers to the presence of people in the crosswalk.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide, multi-lane commercial corridor with a marked crosswalk and a bus shelter. The lack of physical protection such as a median or curb extensions, combined with the wide roadway, creates a high-exposure crossing for pedestrians.
